visual_blocks.heading: 9.2 Kantian autonomy
visual_blocks.preview: **EXAM-READY LINE:** For Kant, an act has moral worth when performed from a rationally self-legislated duty, not from fear of divine punishment or hope of reward.

visual_blocks.heading: 9.3 Natural law and theistic moral realism
visual_blocks.preview: **EXAM-READY LINE:** Natural-law ethics avoids crude voluntarism by grounding moral norms in the rational order of created nature, though it must still explain disputed accounts of human flourishing.

visual_blocks.preview: **EXAM-READY LINE:** Religion can intensify moral motivation through identity, exemplars, community and accountability, but religiosity is neither necessary nor sufficient for moral conduct.
